items.title: No local data on how often the rule would fire and be overridden
items.whyItMatters: Workload for requesters and the laboratory depends on firing and override rates in these practices.
items.opportunity: Run the rule in six practices for four months and record every hold and override.

items.title: Safety of held requests is unproven locally
items.whyItMatters: The network committee asked for a safety review; 200 reviewed holds elsewhere cannot exclude rare harm (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Review every held request followed by a treatment change or an override without an accepted reason.

items.title: Acceptability is uncertain
items.whyItMatters: Many clinicians see diabetes rules as interference (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Test the one-sentence comment and survey requesters at the end of the pilot.

items.title: Patients with barriers to repeat blood draws
items.whyItMatters: For people who travel far or need interpreters, a held test that is later overridden means another visit.
items.opportunity: Record how many overridden holds needed a second draw and report by practice rurality.

reevaluation: The gaps confirm a feasibility pilot with explicit progression criteria and a safety review, not a comparison of effectiveness.
summary: Four gaps; local firing and override data and safety are high severity.
